findings.title: Pages with no meta description
findings.problem: 38 pages have no meta description, so Google writes the snippet itself by pulling an arbitrary sentence from the page.
findings.why: An auto-generated snippet rarely leads with the benefit or the offer, which costs click-through even when the ranking is good.
findings.recommendation: Write a benefit-led description of 120–160 characters that answers what the page offers and why to click.

findings.title: Duplicate meta descriptions
findings.problem: 24 pages reuse the same description, typically a category-level sentence copied across every product in the range.
findings.why: Repeated snippets make near-identical results in the SERP, so shoppers cannot tell your pages apart before clicking.
findings.recommendation: Give each page a description naming its own specification, use case or audience.

findings.title: Descriptions shorter than 120 characters
findings.problem: 42 descriptions fall well under the space Google renders, leaving most of the snippet empty.
findings.why: Short descriptions waste free advertising space and give the searcher less reason to choose your result.
findings.recommendation: Expand each one toward 120–160 characters with a concrete benefit and a call to action.

findings.title: Descriptions longer than 160 characters
findings.problem: 34 descriptions exceed the rendered width and are cut off mid-sentence with an ellipsis.
findings.why: The truncated tail is usually where the call to action sits, so the snippet ends on nothing persuasive.
findings.recommendation: Lead with the value proposition and keep each description within 160 characters.

findings.title: Generic or repeated alt text
findings.problem: 104 images reuse the same alt text — typically the bare product name repeated across every shot in the gallery.
findings.why: Identical alt text tells a screen-reader user nothing about what changes between images, and adds no new context for search.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate each image by what it depicts: front view, in use, size reference, packaging.

findings.title: Empty alt attributes on meaningful images
findings.problem: 96 images declare alt="" — correct for decorative images, but these carry product or editorial meaning.
findings.why: An empty alt tells assistive technology to skip the image entirely, so genuinely useful content is silently dropped.
findings.recommendation: Keep alt="" only for purely decorative graphics; describe everything a sighted user would gain from.

findings.title: Conflicting canonical tags
findings.problem: 22 URLs declare a canonical that points somewhere unexpected — at a filtered variant, a paginated page, or back and forth between two URLs.
findings.why: A conflicting canonical tells search engines to consolidate ranking signals onto the wrong URL, so the page you want ranking is suppressed.
findings.recommendation: Point each canonical at the single preferred URL and make sure that target self-references.

findings.title: Duplicate URLs without consolidation
findings.problem: 42 URLs serve substantially the same content — filter and sort parameters generating a crawlable page per combination.
findings.why: Duplicate URLs split ranking signals and burn crawl budget on pages that will never rank in their own right.
findings.recommendation: Canonicalise parameter URLs to the clean collection URL and keep faceted combinations out of the crawl.

findings.title: Pages with no canonical tag
findings.problem: 18 URLs emit no canonical link element, leaving consolidation entirely to search-engine inference.
findings.why: Without an explicit canonical, any future parameter or protocol variation can be treated as a separate page.
findings.recommendation: Emit a self-referencing canonical on every indexable template by default.

findings.title: Redirects that end in a 404
findings.problem: 12 redirects resolve to a destination that no longer exists, so the visitor lands on an error page.
findings.why: A broken redirect wastes every inbound link pointing at the old URL and sends shoppers to a dead end mid-journey.
findings.recommendation: Repoint each redirect at the closest live equivalent, or the parent collection if the product is gone.

findings.title: Redirect chains and loops
findings.problem: 24 URLs pass through two or more hops before reaching their destination, and two of them loop back on themselves.
findings.why: Each hop adds latency and dilutes link equity; a loop never resolves at all and is dropped from the index.
findings.recommendation: Flatten every chain to a single 301 from the original URL straight to the final destination.

findings.title: Invalid or unstable URL handles
findings.problem: 8 handles contain uppercase characters, underscores or auto-generated numeric suffixes such as -1 and -copy.
findings.why: Unstable handles change when products are re-saved, quietly creating new URLs and orphaning the originals.
findings.recommendation: Normalise handles to lowercase hyphenated slugs and redirect the old form once.

findings.title: Pages blocked by robots.txt
findings.problem: 12 URLs are disallowed in robots.txt yet still listed in the sitemap, so you are submitting pages you have told crawlers to ignore.
findings.why: A blocked URL cannot be read, so it cannot rank — and the contradictory signal wastes crawl budget on every visit.
findings.recommendation: Decide per URL: either remove the disallow rule, or drop the URL from the sitemap.

findings.title: Indexable pages carrying a noindex tag
findings.problem: 10 pages emit a noindex robots directive, including two revenue-generating collection pages.
findings.why: A noindex directive removes the page from search results entirely, regardless of how well it is otherwise optimised.
findings.recommendation: Remove noindex from every page that should rank, and confirm the change before the next crawl.

findings.title: Submitted pages that are not indexed
findings.problem: 36 URLs are in the sitemap and crawlable but have not been indexed — typically thin, near-duplicate or newly published pages.
findings.why: Pages that are crawled but never indexed usually signal a quality or duplication problem rather than a technical one.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the content, add internal links from established pages, and remove genuine near-duplicates.

findings.title: Indexable pages missing from the sitemap
findings.problem: 18 indexable URLs are absent from the sitemap, mostly newer blog posts and support pages.
findings.why: Omitted pages still get found through internal links, but discovery is slower and less reliable for deep pages.
findings.recommendation: Include every indexable, canonical URL in the sitemap and regenerate it on publish.

findings.problem: No llms.txt exists at the domain root and agents.md omits 18 directives (policies, catalog endpoints, support contact). 42 pages are blocked for AI crawlers.
findings.why: Answer engines and shopping agents cannot discover brand policies or catalog structure, so the store is skipped for agentic queries.
evidence: No llms.txt exists at the domain root and agents.md omits 18 directives (policies, catalog endpoints, support contact). 42 pages are blocked for AI crawlers.

details.issueType: llms.txt is missing and agents.md is incomplete

details.summary: 1,042 of 1,284 products meet the current agentic commerce attributes standard.

findings.title: Agent-facing attributes missing on 242 products
findings.problem: Returns window, shipping class, subscription eligibility and GTIN are absent from product markup on 242 products; 86 lack a purchase-action signal entirely.
findings.why: AI shopping agents will not recommend or transact on products whose purchase terms they cannot read.
evidence: Returns window, shipping class, subscription eligibility and GTIN are absent from product markup on 242 products; 86 lack a purchase-action signal entirely.

details.summary: 742 of 1,284 products meet the current answerable q&a + faq schema standard.

findings.title: No FAQPage schema on 318 PDPs; 12 recurring pre-sale questions unanswered
findings.problem: The support inbox shows the same 12 questions (battery life, waterproofing, device compatibility) but the PDPs neither answer them nor expose FAQPage markup.
findings.why: Assistants fall back to generic answers — or a competitor whose page answers the question — for high-intent questions.
evidence: The support inbox shows the same 12 questions (battery life, waterproofing, device compatibility) but the PDPs neither answer them nor expose FAQPage markup.

details.issueType: No FAQPage schema on 318 PDPs; 12 recurring pre-sale questions unanswered

evidence: 182 feed rows are incomplete and 76 lack GTIN/MPN; no feed variant carries the agent-specific fields (returns, shipping, availability windows).

findings.title: 312 products have no reviews; no UGC on PDPs
findings.problem: Post-purchase review requests are not automated, so 312 products show an empty rating block and trust badges cover only 61% of PDPs.
findings.why: Unreviewed PDPs convert materially worse than reviewed ones; badges and UGC close the confidence gap.

findings.problem: 86 of 284 return requests still go through support email; label generation and refund-to-store-credit are not self-serve.
findings.why: Manual returns cost support time and a slow, opaque returns process suppresses first-time purchase confidence.

findings.title: 314 orders shipped without branded tracking
findings.problem: Branded tracking covers 58% of orders; the rest redirect customers to carrier sites and only 64% receive proactive delivery updates.

details.summary: 1,671 of 1,840 cod orders meet the current cod checkout quality standard.

findings.title: COD checkout lacks OTP verification and RTO risk gating
findings.problem: COD is offered on 58% of eligible orders with no phone OTP; 18% of COD orders are refused at the door.
findings.why: Every refused COD delivery is a paid round-trip; OTP + risk scoring typically halves refusal rates.
evidence: COD is offered on 58% of eligible orders with no phone OTP; 18% of COD orders are refused at the door.

details.issueType: COD checkout lacks OTP verification and RTO risk gating
